messages:
Jess: FYI just heard from Sales — Skyline reporting throughput collapse this morning after the 03:10 canary. Their QPS dropped ~60% and app-level timeouts spiked. They want ETA and whether this is on Redwood or their config.
Sam: Customer logs attached to ticket #9872. They see many 429s and backend timeouts. Happened right after model switch to rwd-v2-optimized.
Sam: snippet from customer: ```2026-03-18T03:12:08Z ERROR request_id=abc123 send: upstream timeout after 4500ms``` 
Anita: @Jess @Sam tagging eng-runtime. Initial guess: KV cache invalidation + default batching config mismatch for that model variant. Also the new kernel path changed latency distribution.
Liam: If KV warms slowly, throughput can dip for a while. Can we check recent rollout throttles/traffic split? deploy-bot: can you paste deploy info?
deploy-bot: Deployment rwd-v2-optimized rolled to canary at 2026-03-18T03:05Z by pipeline #deploy-2045. Traffic split 5% -> 50% at 03:10 by autoscale policy.
Raj: Skyline is Dedicated; their SLA is 99.9% p95. If their traffic was ramped, routing should have fallback to previous variant. Do we have fallback logs?
Anita: searching traces now. Early sign: p50 unchanged, p95 jumped from 180ms -> 1.8s for canary requests. Batching latency up. Possible batching threshold miscalibrated for shorter sequences.
Maya: OK product decision needed: is this urgent hotfix (roll back canary) vs scoped backlog item (fix batching heuristics + rollout gating). What customer impact do we log to prioritize?
Jess: Customer says user-facing errors and revenue impact. Sales requests immediate rollback or 100% traffic rollback for Skyline. They prefer rollback to unblock.
Liam: We can flip routing for Skyline to previous model variant and lock canary for them. Low risk and fast. Need a ticket to change routing policy (route-by-customer override).
Sam: I've already asked Skyline for exact traffic curves. They reported a sudden spike at 03:09-03:14 as external marketing test. QPS went from 150 -> 1200 briefly.
Raj: That spike explains batching path hitting worst-case. For backlog, we need: (1) model variant performance profile per seq-length, (2) adaptive batching thresholds, (3) rollout gating by recent p95 telemetry.
Maya: Acceptance criteria for backlog task: measurable fix that keeps p95 < 300ms under 1k QPS for short sequences, unit tests for batching heuristic, rollout policy that auto-rolls back when p95 > 2x baseline for 5m. Estimate scope: 2 sprints cross-team.
Anita: I'll open an eng-runtime bug with logs + heatmap. For immediate triage: can we route Skyline off the canary now? @Liam can you do the routing override and notify Sales?
Liam: On it. I'll apply customer override to previous variant and set a short-term rule to prevent automatic ramp. ETA 10m.
Jess: Thanks. I'll tell Skyline we're switching them back and apologize. Sales asked for a postmortem and timeline when fix will be prioritized.
Maya: Postmortem + prioritized backlog card required. If patch is >2sprints we commit to a roadmap item and set customer expectation.
Sam: Ticket created: PRODUCT-1347 (Customer throughput regression intake) with customer logs and impact notes.
Raj: Also request: capture a synthetic replay with Skyline payloads and run locally against both variants to reproduce.
Anita: Good call — I'll queue a replay job and attach perf artifacts.
Liam: Routing override done at 1765432359. Monitoring shows Skyline p95 back to baseline ~280ms.
Jess: Customer notified, they confirm reduced errors. Sales wants timeline and potential credits. I'll coordinate with finance later.
Maya: Thanks team. Next actions: Anita -> runtime ticket + replay artifacts; Raj -> perf validation plan; Eng -> batching heuristics spike analysis; Product -> backlog card + customer comms. Close loop in this thread when all items created.
Sam: noted, will update PRODUCT-1347 and ping when artifacts are attached.
